system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented Global Order: Energy Shocks, Great-Power Frictions and AI Turbulence
system_description.narrative_summary: A multipolar international system is in volatile flux as regional wars and proxy attacks (notably in the Middle East and Ukraine) drive energy-market shocks and realign security calculations. Great-power competition (US, China, Russia) is spilling into trade, technology and diplomacy, while runaway advances in AI — accompanied by espionage and export-control battles — create a new transnational domain of strategic rivalry. Domestic political instability in major democracies and stresses in financial and commodity markets amplify feedbacks across the system, making policy coordination and crisis management harder.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and alliances (NATO, EU, G7), non-state armed actors (Houthis, Iran-backed militias), global energy and shipping routes (Strait of Hormuz), international financial and commodity markets, major technology firms and AI ecosystems, information and intelligence networks, transnational supply chains, and public political dynamics (elections, protests).
system_description.super_system: The global political-economic order (the integrated international system of states, markets, institutions, and transnational technological infrastructures).
adjacent_subsystems: Regional Middle East security and energy flows

variables.name: Russia-Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain locked in a high‑intensity conventional and asymmetric war as Moscow pursues territorial aims and Kyiv adapts with strikes and defensive measures that are reshaping battlefield dynamics.

variables.name: Strait of Hormuz & Middle East escalation
variables.description: Iran, Iran‑backed Houthi forces and Saudi Arabia are engaged in escalating maritime and land attacks centered on the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf shipping lanes, raising maritime risk and spurring oil‑price volatility.

variables.name: US political realignment and alliance strain
variables.description: Political turbulence inside the United States is producing rapid shifts in sanctions, trade policy and alliance behaviour — including waivers and threats to intelligence‑sharing — that are eroding predictability in global commitments.

variables.name: China tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: China is tightening export controls and bolstering domestic champions while facing growing regulatory and trade pushback from major markets over AI, chips and clean‑tech supply chains, accelerating strategic competition in critical technologies.

variables.name: European political and economic turbulence
variables.description: France and the European Union are experiencing intense social unrest, fiscal strain and political fragmentation that weaken governance and complicate collective responses to external shocks and policy coordination.
